display.title: Display & presence
display.subtitle: Brightness, night light, presence and camera

kiosk_dashboard.title: Main dashboard (kiosk)
kiosk_dashboard.desc: The Home Assistant dashboard that stays on screen. Required before you can lock the kiosk.
kiosk_dashboard.help: Opened after a restart, when you press Home and when the lock starts. Paste the address from your browser.
kiosk_dashboard.kw: url, link, lovelace, page, default, wall panel, address, home screen, path, kiosk dashboard

glance_enabled.title: Show an idle screen
glance_enabled.desc: When nobody touches or stands near the tablet for a while, show a calm screen instead of the main dashboard.
glance_enabled.kw: screensaver, at a glance, idle, clock, screen saver

glance_dashboard.title: Idle dashboard (at a glance)
glance_dashboard.desc: Optional second dashboard for the idle screen, e.g. weather and temperatures. Empty = built-in clock screen.
glance_dashboard.help: Build it in Home Assistant with any cards (weather, cameras, floor temperatures). A touch or someone nearby returns to the main dashboard. Leave empty for the built-in clock screen.
glance_dashboard.kw: url, link, lovelace, screensaver, weather, idle dashboard, glance dashboard, address

glance_after.title: Show the idle screen after
glance_after.desc: How long nobody uses or stands near the tablet.

lockdown.title: Lock the kiosk
lockdown.desc: Keeps the dashboard on screen and blocks other apps, the notification shade and recents.
lockdown.kw: lockdown, lock, kiosk mode, block, pin, lock task, pinning

pin.title: PIN
pin.desc: Tap the top-left corner 5 times on the locked screen, then enter your PIN.

allowed_apps.title: Allowed apps
allowed_apps.desc: Other apps that may be opened while the kiosk is locked (the Home Assistant app and the keyboard are always allowed).

protection.title: Kiosk protection
protection.desc: How strongly the lock is enforced: device owner (strongest) or the accessibility guard.
protection.kw: device owner, accessibility, enforcement, lock task, adb, dpm, guard

home_app.title: Start automatically
home_app.desc: Starts after a reboot and brings the Home Assistant app back if it closes or crashes (acts as the home app).
home_app.kw: launcher, boot, autostart, home app, crash, recover, startup, default home

keep_screen_on.title: Keep the screen on
keep_screen_on.desc: Stops the screen from switching off by itself.
keep_screen_on.kw: awake, sleep, timeout, screen off, wake lock

companion_app.title: Home Assistant app
companion_app.desc: The official Home Assistant companion app that shows your dashboard.

brightness_mode.title: Brightness control
brightness_mode.desc: Manual leaves brightness alone. Auto follows day and night. Day or Night forces one of them.
brightness_mode.kw: auto dim, dimming, night mode, day mode, automatic, backlight

day_level.title: Day brightness
day_level.desc: While the tablet is in use or someone is near.

auto_dim.title: Dim when idle
auto_dim.desc: Lower the brightness when nobody uses or stands near the tablet.

day_dim_level.title: Idle brightness
day_dim_level.desc: Brightness while dimmed during the day.

dim_after.title: Dim after
dim_after.desc: How long without touch or presence before dimming.

night_start.title: Night starts
night_start.desc: From this time the night brightness is used. Home Assistant can also switch night mode directly with the enter_night_mode and exit_night_mode actions.
night_start.kw: schedule, sleep, bedtime, hours, enter_night_mode, exit_night_mode, automation

night_end.title: Night ends
night_end.desc: From this time the day brightness is used again.

night_level.title: Night brightness
night_level.desc: Very dim base brightness at night.

night_light.title: Night light
night_light.desc: Brighten the screen a little when someone walks past, so you can see the floor.
night_light.kw: nightlight, walk past, floor, presence, path light

night_light_level.title: Night light brightness
night_light_level.desc: Brightness while someone is near at night.

night_touch_level.title: Brightness after a touch
night_touch_level.desc: Brightness for a moment after you touch the screen at night.

night_hold.title: Keep after a touch
night_hold.desc: How long the touch brightness stays.

presence_sources.title: Presence sources
presence_sources.desc: Who counts as "near the tablet": Home Assistant presence sensors and/or the camera.
presence_sources.help: Choose presence sensors in Home Assistant: Settings → Devices & services → HA Sidecar → Configure. The camera below is optional.
presence_sources.kw: mmwave, pir, sensor, occupancy, motion, entities

presence_hold.title: Keep "present" for
presence_hold.desc: How long presence is kept after the last detection.

camera_presence.title: Detect presence with the camera
camera_presence.desc: Notices movement near the tablet. Nothing is recorded, stored or sent; a notification shows while it runs.
camera_presence.kw: camera, motion, privacy, detect, webcam, front camera

camera_status.title: Camera status
camera_status.desc: Whether the presence camera is running and sees movement.

camera_sensitivity.title: Sensitivity
camera_sensitivity.desc: Higher notices smaller movements (and more false alarms).

connection.title: Connection
connection.desc: The link to your Home Assistant server (pairing token).
connection.kw: pair, token, url, server, unpair, reconnect, integration, link

theme.title: Theme
theme.desc: Light, dark, follow the system, or dark only at night.
theme.kw: dark mode, light mode, night mode, colors, appearance

device_owner.title: Device owner
device_owner.desc: Optional, strongest kiosk lock. Needs a one-time adb command on a freshly reset tablet.
device_owner.kw: dpm, adb, provision, managed, lock task

update.title: Android system update
update.desc: Opens the system update screen and, with the accessibility guard, taps through it.
update.kw: os update, upgrade, security patch, version, firmware

run_setup.title: Run the setup wizard again
run_setup.desc: Walks through connection, dashboard, PIN and permissions step by step.
run_setup.kw: wizard, onboarding, guide, setup, reset, first run, help

raw_brightness.title: Brightness as 0–255
raw_brightness.desc: Show and set brightness levels as raw Android values (0–255) instead of percent.

pair_ha.title: Pair with Home Assistant
pair_ha.desc: Start pairing so Home Assistant can find this tablet.
pair_ha.kw: pair, discover, mdns, zeroconf, code, add, connect

network_status.title: Current network
network_status.desc: Where this tablet is and which address it uses.
network_status.kw: wifi, vpn, ethernet, network, address, route

internal_url.title: Internal address
internal_url.desc: Used at home, on a home network, VPN or Ethernet marked as home.

external_url.title: External address
external_url.desc: Used everywhere else. Leave empty to always use the internal address.
external_url.kw: url, remote, nabu casa, domain, external, internet

home_networks.title: Home Wi-Fi networks
home_networks.desc: Networks where the internal address is used. Reading the Wi-Fi name needs the location permission.

vpn_is_home.title: VPN counts as home
vpn_is_home.desc: Use the internal address while a VPN is connected.

ethernet_is_home.title: Ethernet counts as home
ethernet_is_home.desc: Use the internal address on a wired connection.

connection_policy.title: Keep the connection
connection_policy.desc: Always stay connected, or only while on a home network.
connection_policy.kw: persistent, always, home only, battery, vpn, network

pin.dialog_intro: At least 4 digits. You will enter it by tapping the top-left corner of the locked screen 5 times.
pin.required_desc: Required before the kiosk can be locked.

page.title: Enter PIN to leave the kiosk
page.locked: Too many tries. Try again in {seconds} s

lock.locked_only_ha: Locked. Only the Home Assistant app can be used.
lock.locked_with_allowed: Locked. Only the Home Assistant app and your allowed apps can be used.
lock.err_dashboard: Choose the kiosk dashboard first (Kiosk → Dashboards).
lock.err_protection: Turn on the accessibility guard or make this tablet a device owner first.

allowed.intro: While the kiosk is locked only these apps can be opened. The Home Assistant app and the keyboard are always allowed.

prot.device_owner_desc: Strongest: Android itself blocks the system UI.
prot.accessibility_desc: Good: other apps are sent back. Device owner is stronger.
prot.none_desc: Turn on the accessibility guard or become device owner to lock the kiosk.

home.active: Active. This app is the default home app.
home.choose: Almost done: choose "HA Sidecar" as the default home app in Android.

needs_attention_sub.one: {} thing to fix before this works properly
needs_attention_sub.other: {} things to fix before this works properly

home.all_set_desc: The kiosk is ready. Use the lock above to start it.
home.brightness_unmanaged: Brightness is not managed (Display → Brightness control)
home.extras_desc: This device reports sensors and rings alarms for Home Assistant.

companion.missing: Not found. Install the Home Assistant companion app and sign in to your server.

camera.permission_desc: Allow camera access so movement can be detected.

owner.active_desc: This tablet is a device owner: Android itself hides and blocks the system UI.

overlay.title: Display over other apps
overlay.why: Lets the sidecar bring the Home Assistant app back to the front, track touches for dimming and show the hidden PIN corner.
overlay.hint: On the next screen switch on "Allow display over other apps" for HA Sidecar.

accessibility.title: Accessibility guard
accessibility.why: Keeps other apps, the notification shade and the recents screen away from the dashboard when this tablet is not a device owner, and reports which app is in front. It does not read your screen.
accessibility.hint: Open "Installed apps" / "Downloaded apps", choose the HA Sidecar kiosk guard and switch it on. If Android says "restricted setting": App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then try again.

write_settings.title: Modify system settings
write_settings.why: Needed to change the screen brightness for auto dimming, the night light and remote brightness.
write_settings.hint: On the next screen switch on "Allow modifying system settings".

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.why: Alarms and the camera indicator are shown as notifications, and Android needs one to keep the sidecar running.

battery.title: No battery restrictions
battery.why: Stops Android from pausing the sidecar in the background, which would silence alarms and drop the Home Assistant connection.
battery.hint: Choose "All apps", find HA Sidecar and set it to "Don't optimize".

full_screen_intent.title: Full-screen alarms
full_screen_intent.why: Lets a ringing alarm take over the screen, also while the kiosk is locked.
full_screen_intent.hint: On the next screen switch on "Allow full-screen notifications".

dashboard.invalid: That is not a dashboard address. Paste the address from your browser, e.g. https://home.example.org/lovelace/wall-panel
dashboard.host_mismatch: That address is on {host}, not on your paired Home Assistant ({paired}). Only the path "{path}" is used.

protection.title: Kiosk protection
protection.intro: Two ways to keep other apps away from the dashboard. You can use both.
protection.accessibility_desc: Works on any tablet. Sends other apps back and closes the notification shade within a moment.
protection.owner_desc: Android itself hides and blocks the system UI. Needs a factory-reset tablet with no accounts and a computer with adb.
protection.how_steps:
1. Factory reset the tablet and skip adding any account.
2. Install this app and the Home Assistant app.
3. Enable USB debugging and, on a computer, run:
protection.warning: A device owner cannot be removed afterwards except by a factory reset. Fire tablets are not supported.

search.title: Search settings
search.suggestions: night light, dashboard, dim, PIN, camera, permission, brightness, idle screen, theme, update
search.none_hint: Try a shorter word, like "dim", "night" or "url".

link.title: Not connected to Home Assistant
link.detail: Remote control, sensors and alarms in Home Assistant need the connection. Local features keep working.

link_rejected.title: Home Assistant rejected the token
link_rejected.detail: Create a new pairing token in the integration and pair again.

companion.title: Home Assistant app not installed
companion.detail: The kiosk shows your dashboard with the official Home Assistant companion app. Install it and sign in.

dashboard.title: Choose the kiosk dashboard
dashboard.detail: Paste the address of the dashboard that should stay on screen. Lockdown needs it.

pin.title: Set a PIN
pin.detail: The PIN is the only way to leave the locked kiosk on the tablet.

protection.title: No kiosk protection available
protection.detail: Turn on the accessibility guard, or make this tablet a device owner for the strongest lock.

home_app.title: Start automatically after a restart
home_app.detail: Act as the home app so the kiosk comes back after a reboot or when the Home Assistant app closes.

alarms.title: Alarms
alarms.intro: These alarms ring on this tablet, also while the kiosk is locked. Home Assistant can create, snooze and stop them too.
alarms.empty_desc: Tap "Add alarm" or create one from a Home Assistant automation.
alarms.swipe_hint: Swipe an alarm to the left to delete it.
alarms.label: Label (optional)
alarms.mute_desc: Silence all alarms, for example while you are away. They keep their schedule.
alarms.muted_forever: Muted until you turn this off

welcome.title: Turn this tablet into a Home Assistant display
welcome.intro: HA Sidecar adds what the Home Assistant app does not: a lockable kiosk, smart brightness, alarms and extra sensors. Setup takes about five minutes.
welcome.b1_text: Keeps your dashboard on screen. Leave it with a PIN.
welcome.b2_text: Dims when idle, night light when someone walks past.
welcome.b3_text: Alarms that Home Assistant can set, plus touch, camera and security sensors.

connect.title: Connect to Home Assistant
connect.intro: This tablet pairs with the HA Sidecar integration in Home Assistant. Both stay on your network; nothing is typed by hand.
connect.s1_text: In HACS add the HA Sidecar repository (Custom repositories → Integration) and restart Home Assistant.
connect.s2_text: Press the button below. The tablet now announces itself on your network.
connect.s3_text: The tablet shows up under Settings → Devices & services as discovered. Press Configure, name it, and confirm the number on this screen.
connect.rejected: Home Assistant rejected the token. Check it and try again.
connect.manual_title: Enter the address and token manually
connect.manual_text: For older setups. New setups pair as described above.

mode.title: What is this device for?
mode.intro: You can change this later by running the setup again.
mode.kiosk_text: A tablet that permanently shows a Home Assistant dashboard, locked with a PIN.
mode.extras_text: A phone or tablet you also use normally. No lock; Home Assistant gets extra sensors and can set alarms.

companion.title: The Home Assistant app
companion.intro: The kiosk shows your dashboard with the official Home Assistant companion app. HA Sidecar keeps it on screen.
companion.missing_text: Install "Home Assistant" from Google Play, or the minimal build from the Home Assistant GitHub / F-Droid.
companion.b1_text: Open the app once, sign in to your server and let it finish loading. Then come back here.
companion.b2_text: In its settings, turn on fullscreen so no bars show. Do not set it as the launcher; HA Sidecar does that.

dashboard.title: Which dashboard stays on screen?
dashboard.intro: Open the dashboard in a browser, copy its address and paste it here. Only the path is kept.
dashboard.later: You can add an idle dashboard (weather, temperatures) later under Kiosk → Dashboards.

pin.title: Choose a PIN
pin.intro: The PIN is the only way to leave the locked kiosk on the tablet itself.
pin.b1_text: On the locked screen tap the top-left corner 5 times, then enter the PIN. After 5 wrong tries there is a short waiting time.
pin.b2_text: You can also unlock remotely from Home Assistant. Remote locking needs a PIN to exist.

protection.title: How strong should the lock be?
protection.intro: Android has two ways to keep other apps away from the dashboard. Device owner is strongest; the accessibility guard works on any tablet.
protection.owner_text: Needs a factory-reset tablet with no accounts and a one-time computer command. Optional.
protection.guard_text: Sends other apps and the notification shade away within a moment. Does not read your screen.
protection.command_help: Run it once on a computer with the tablet connected by USB debugging. It cannot be undone except by a factory reset.
protection.none: Without either, the kiosk cannot be locked.

permissions.title: Allow what the kiosk needs
permissions.intro: Tap Grant, follow the Android screen that opens, then come back. This list updates by itself.
permissions.skip_help: You can skip anything and finish it later; the Home screen lists what is still missing.

startup.title: Start by itself
startup.intro: Let HA Sidecar be the home app. After a reboot, or if the Home Assistant app closes or crashes, Android returns to HA Sidecar, which opens the dashboard again.

display.title: Brightness
display.intro: Should the display manage its own brightness? Every detail can be fine-tuned later under Display.
display.smart_text: Bright by day, dims when nobody uses it, very dim at night with a night light when someone walks past.
display.manual_text: The sidecar never changes the screen brightness.
display.note: Night hours are 22:00 to 06:30 by default. Presence sensors are chosen in the Home Assistant integration options.

done.intro_kiosk: Lock the kiosk now, or open the app first and look around. You can change everything later, and search finds any setting.
done.intro_extras: Home Assistant now gets sensors and can set alarms on this device.
done.intro_open: A few things are still open. You can finish them later from the Home screen.

timers.label: Name (optional)
timers.invalid: Choose a time between 1 second and 99 hours.

pairing.found_auto: Open Home Assistant: this tablet appears as a discovered device. Press Configure there.
pairing.manual: Not found? Add the integration HA Sidecar in Home Assistant and enter this address and code:
pairing.locked: Too many wrong codes. Pairing was switched off; start it again.
pairing.request_text: Check that Home Assistant shows the same number, then allow.

net.allow_location: Allow location to read the Wi-Fi name
